pl-l4d33c4-d1e115.summary: Asks whether it was lawful under the Law to have several wives.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e118.summary: Cites Deuteronomy: you shall not have many wives who allure your soul.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e124.summary: Quotes Augustine: Solomon clearly transgressed this, while David had several and did not, since it was permitted to have several, not many who allure the soul; 'lest his heart be lifted up' seems to forbid foreign wives. Multiplying wives was generally forbidden; kings were permitted several, not many.
claims: Kings were permitted several wives, not many.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e134.summary: States that when the fullness of time came and Christ's grace spread everywhere, the law of marriage was restored to its earlier and more honorable institution, that one man be joined to one woman in the figure of Christ and the Church.
claims: Under grace marriage returned to monogamy, figuring Christ and the Church.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e146.summary: Adds that office is no longer chosen by succession of lineage but by perfection of life and sincerity of knowledge, virginity is preferred to fertility, and continence is enjoined on priests.
claims: Virginity is now preferred to fertility.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e152.summary: States that virginity of mind is better than of flesh.
claims: Virginity of mind surpasses that of flesh.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e155.summary: Quotes Ambrose: it is more tolerable to have a virgin mind than a virgin flesh; both are good if possible; if not, let us be chaste to God rather than men. A virgin can be prostituted but not adulterated; brothels do not defame chastity, but chastity abolishes the infamy of the place.
claims: A virgin can be violated in body but not in mind.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e167.summary: Adds Ambrose: the flesh cannot be corrupted unless the mind is first corrupted.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e173.summary: Adds Isidore: the body cannot be corrupted unless the mind is first corrupted; when the soul is clean of contagion, the flesh does not sin.
claims: The flesh does not sin when the soul is clean.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e180.summary: Explains that the end of the chapter shows how it is true that the body cannot be corrupted unless the soul is first corrupted: namely, by sin.
claims: Corruption here means corruption by sin.

pl-l4d33c4-d1e183.summary: Notes Augustine: as it is holier to die of hunger than eat food offered to idols, so it is holier to die childless than seek offspring by unlawful union; yet however men are born, if they do not follow their parents' vices and worship God rightly, they will be honorable and saved, since the seed is God's creature and only its misuse is evil.
claims: Childlessness is better than unlawful offspring.
Children of unlawful unions can be saved.

pl-l4d33c4.summary: Asks whether several wives were permitted under the Law: Deuteronomy forbids the king many wives who would turn his heart; Augustine says Solomon transgressed, David did not, since several were permitted, not many, and foreign wives forbidden. In the fullness of time, marriage was restored to its first institution, one to one, figuring Christ and the Church; office no longer follows lineage but life and knowledge, virginity is preferred to fertility, and continence enjoined on priests. Virginity of mind is better than of flesh: Ambrose says a virgin can be prostituted but not adulterated, and the flesh is corrupted only if the mind is first corrupted. Augustine: it is holier to die childless than to seek offspring by unlawful union; yet any child, however born, is God's creature and can be saved.
claims: Under the Law several, not many, wives were permitted to kings.
Under grace marriage returned to one man and one woman.
Virginity is now preferred to fertility, and continence enjoined on priests.
Virginity of mind is better than of flesh.
Children of unlawful unions are God's creatures and can be saved.
